notes: Coder B was more granular (79 vs 66 units), which accounts for 14 kept B-only units (split sentences such as the SAS exception, 'not a replacement for your own thinking', detector bias vs. evidence standard, FERPA vs. de-identification, the timing of communication, the copyright caveat). Two A-only units ('This includes faculty use', 'You are responsible for the accuracy of your assignments') are real statements and were kept. One B-only unit was dropped (the 'culmination of input from multiple faculty committees' sentence, not about AI). Main disagreements: (1) phase for syllabus-statement sentences (A course-start, B during-work), resolved as course-start for statements that tell students the course rule and during-work for conduct rules inside assignments; (2) policy_type: P55 vs P87 for the learning-benefits sentence (P87, it states benefits and risks), P101 vs P46 for faculty review of AI findings and the opt-out right (P101 for conditions on AI-assisted grading, P46 kept for 'AI will not replace your own evaluation'), P62 vs P04 and P54 vs P09 in the graduate guidance (P62 for committee authorization, P09 for the regular-communication duty), P56 vs P02 for the USNH 'supports responsible exploration' preamble (P56); (3) actor differences (instructor vs admin for the university's preference for guidance over prohibition: admin; all vs admin for the reporting procedure: all); (4) unit_stance differences on rationale sentences (neutral) and on the 'own ideas and words' bullet (restrict); (5) document stance for the USNH bulletin (A delegates, B permit), resolved as permit because it states support and conditions for all use and only refers academic integrity to institutions. Shares are over matched units; stance agreement is over the 3 documents.
